items.prompt: Where do production secrets belong on an n8n canvas?
options: In the workflow JSON, committed to the repo
In the HTTP node's URL, base64-encoded
In environment variables (or the encrypted credential store) referenced by name — a secret exists in exactly two places: the env source and the platform's encrypted store
In a pinned note on the canvas for the team to see
items.explanation: Env-var references keep the canvas shareable, the repo clean, and rotation a re-pointing exercise. Never in node parameters, never in exports, never in receipts. (obj-09-a)

items.prompt: Which retry policy is the production posture?
options: ≤2 retries with exponential backoff on 5xx/timeout; NEVER retry 4xx — a 403 retried is still a 403, just later and louder
Unlimited retries every 30 seconds until success
items.explanation: Retries buy resilience against transient noise; on permanent failures they become a self-inflicted denial-of-service with a schedule. (obj-09-a)

items.prompt: A per-run token budget is checked by the policy node mid-run and found exceeded. What happens?
options: ESCALATE [over_budget] — the loop stops itself, the receipt preserves what was pending, the digest tells the human with numbers
The workflow silently skips the expensive call
The error workflow retries the run with a higher budget
The budget resets automatically and the run continues
items.explanation: The ledger feeds the rule; the rule escalates with evidence. Silent budget-swallowing would be a drift amplifier — you think you're scanning everything; you're scanning the affordable. (obj-09-b)

items.prompt: What does the running case study print on every receipt about its unit accounting?
options: units_source: the '1 actor run = 1 unit' approximation is DECLARED because per-actor pricing is not yet captured; money stays 'unmeasured' until a price table exists
A fixed euro amount per run
items.explanation: Approximations are declared at the unit, and money is unmeasured-not-guessed until prices are captured — the receipt says which world you are in. (obj-09-b)
